title: Desktop UI and MVVM
summary: Building desktop applications with C# - the choices (WinForms, WPF, WinUI, Avalonia, .NET MAUI), event-driven UI and the UI thread, XAML and data binding, the MVVM pattern with INotifyPropertyChanged, ObservableCollection and ICommand, keeping the UI responsive with async, and testing view models without a window.

cards.q: Why must a UI event handler not run a 5-second calculation directly?
cards.a:
It runs on the UI thread, so the window freezes until it finishes

While the handler runs, the UI thread cannot draw or respond to clicks. Await the work instead (with `Task.Run` for CPU work).

cards.q: What does INotifyPropertyChanged do for data binding?
cards.a:
It raises PropertyChanged when a property changes, so bound controls read the new value

Binding reads a property once; the PropertyChanged event is how the view model tells the controls that a value has changed.

cards.q: In MVVM, where does the rule "the Add button is disabled while the title is empty" belong?
cards.a:
In the view model, as the command's CanExecute

The view model holds the screen's behaviour; the view only binds to it.
